title.narrative: Strengthening protective environment for flood-affected IDPs through Prevention Response to GBV in Baidoa district.

description.narrative: ltpgtIn response to Somalia's recurrent climate crisis, characterized by the current El Niño-induced floods wreaking havoc across the country, particularly in the Southern riverine areas, Baidoa district is experiencing profound challenges. The floods have displaced 22,190 families residing in over 377 IDP camps, with a staggering 83% of affected households headed by women. The figures have caused protection concerns, particularly for women and girls who are disproportionately affected by feminized poverty, limited physical mobility, depleted livelihoods, and disrupted health services resulting from the effects of the river and flash floods, increasing their vulnerability to GBV (Gender-Based Violence) instances. As they continue to be displaced, their living conditions become more precarious, and they may be forced to seek refuge in overcrowded and unsafe locations and opt for the most undesirable mechanisms in meeting their immediate need for other necessities. ltbrgt ltbrgtThe project's interventions are strategically designed to cater to the unique needs of GBV survivors, acknowledging the heightened vulnerability of women and girls in the aftermath of flooding. The multifaceted approach encompasses the distribution of dignity and menstrual kits to 1,000 individuals, prioritizing survivors and those at risk while adhering to a survivor-centered approach aligned with Somalia GBV AoR standards. The provision of the dignity kits is aimed to strengthen the protective environment, prevent and protecting women and girls from risks of violation of their rights, particularly from the risk of gender-based violence. Dignity and menstrual kits will contribute to psycho-social and physical well-being and restoration of dignity to reduce the susceptibility in the IDP camps. At the same time., READO aims to address immediate GBV concerns by providing cash voucher assistance to 300 survivors, employing a case-by-case approach to prevent and mitigate exposure risks. The project also encompasses Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) services for 300 GBV survivors within health facilities, following WHO CMR guidelines and ethical standards. This initiative aims to improve referral mechanisms and encourage survivors to report incidents promptly for a timely and effective response within established protocols. Additionally, READO will undertake case management and psychosocial support for 1,845 GBV survivors and vulnerable individuals, including 1,380 women, 400 girls, 20 men, and 45 boys residing in Baidoa's IDP camps. ltbrgt ltbrgtThe project extends its impact through awareness-raising and outreach activities on service availability, prevention, and mitigation of GBV, with a target audience of 8,500 individuals. Collaboration with other clusters, including WASH, Health, Nutrition, and CCCM, ensures inter-cluster integration, facilitating a holistic approach to support vulnerable communities in meeting various basic needs and services. Coordination with CCCM, in collaboration with the Sub-GBV Working Group and the Ministry of Women and Human Rights at Southwest Cluster, ensures the identification and targeting of beneficiaries, with a particular focus on those affected by drought, aiming to cushion them from further effects of El Niño-induced flooding. ltbrgt ltbrgtWhile aiming to benefit 6,000 individuals directly, the project anticipates an overall reach of approximately 8,500, encompassing both direct and indirect beneficiaries. This comprehensive and survivor-centric approach addresses immediate relief needs and contributes to the long-term resilience and well-being of those affected by GBV in the flood-prone areas of Baidoa, Somalia. The collaborative efforts with various clusters and strategic coordination with relevant authorities underscore the project's commitment to providing a holistic response to the multifaceted challenges posed by the intersection of climate-induced disasters and gender-based violence in the region. ltbrgtlt/pgt
